target: For every pair of positive integers f<g, the greedy sequence starting with exactly f,g and excluding sums of two different actual earlier selected integers has an eventually periodic characteristic function, hence eventually periodic successive gaps.
assumptions: Exactly two positive initial integers f<g; integers below g other than the seeds are skipped.
A representation requires two different actual selected integers; equal residues in different periods may be valid.
Only eventual periodicity is claimed, not minimal periods, optimal transients or arbitrary finite seed sets.
success_criteria: Supply a logically complete written argument for every positive pair f<g, with exact parameter coverage, initial conditions and strict distinctness.
Retain counterexamples to failed extensions and reproducible arithmetic without treating finite scans as a universal proof.
verification_plan: Independent mathematical examination of the full candidate manuscript and necessary appendices remains pending.
Replay the retained printed arithmetic using the portable runner with assertions enabled.
Recheck known-result attribution and the distinction from the broader arbitrary-seed catalogue problem.
